## pplx-04 — Webhook delivery threat model: SSRF, per-tenant egress, retry/dead-letter, replay

- Tool: perplexity-web `search` · Date: 2026-10-03
- Query: "Webhook delivery security threat model for multi-tenant SaaS: SSRF via webhook endpoints (DNS rebinding, redirects, IPv6/IPv4-mapped addresses, cloud metadata 169.254.169.254), per-tenant egress allowlist of destination hosts, re-validating destination at delivery time vs subscription time, secret rotation, replay protection with timestamp tolerance, retry budget and dead-letter queue with manual replay. Cite OWASP SSRF Prevention Cheat Sheet and webhook provider docs (Stripe, GitHub, Svix)."
- Status: provenance (synthesized answer; returned as a table, sources cited inline). Not a primary source; used as threat-model checklist only.

## Answer (verbatim)

"Surface","Threat","Control"
"Tenant-supplied URL","URL parser tricks, unsafe schemes, userinfo, nonstandard ports, or malformed hostnames route requests somewhere unintended","Prefer storing a parsed, normalized destination rather than repeatedly interpreting a raw URL. Require HTTPS and an explicit port policy; reject ambiguous or unsupported URL forms. OWASP advises against accepting complete user URLs when possible and recommends building requests from validated components. cheatsheetseries.owasp"
"DNS lookup and connection","DNS rebinding or a time-of-check/time-of-use gap changes the resolved address between validation and connect","At subscription time, validate syntax and tenant policy. At every delivery, resolve A and AAAA records, reject the destination if any answer is forbidden, and ensure the HTTP client connects to a validated address without re-resolving it. DNS validation at registration alone is not sufficient. OWASP specifically calls out validating all IPv4 and IPv6 answers to address DNS pinning. cheatsheetseries.owasp"
"Address representation","IPv4-mapped IPv6 or alternate IP representations bypass checks that only recognize familiar IPv4 strings","Parse addresses with a tested IP library, normalize them to canonical forms, and classify the normalized address. Check IPv4 and IPv6, including mapped IPv4, loopback, private, link-local, unspecified, multicast, and organization-specific internal ranges."
"Redirect handling","A permitted public URL redirects to a private service or metadata address","Disable automatic redirects. If product requirements demand redirects, treat every hop as a new destination: validate scheme, host, resolved addresses, and port again, and enforce a small redirect limit. OWASP explicitly recommends disabling redirects as an SSRF defense. cheatsheetseries.owasp"
"Cloud and internal network","Requests reach metadata services such as 169.254.169.254, internal APIs, or other tenants’ infrastructure","Block private and link-local destinations, including the metadata address, at both application and network layers. Run delivery workers in an isolated egress network or route through a filtering proxy; do not rely on application checks alone. OWASP lists 169.254.169.254 and private/local ranges among minimum deny-list entries, and Svix recommends a filtering proxy plus network isolation. cheatsheetseries.owasp+1"
"Shared worker and tenant data","A compromised endpoint or misrouted job receives another tenant’s payload or headers","Bind each queued delivery to immutable tenant, endpoint, and event identifiers. Scope authorization and secret lookup to that tenant and endpoint. Do not forward ambient credentials, internal cookies, or authorization headers."
"Retry and manual replay","Retries create duplicate effects; operators replay to a modified or unsafe destination","Make deliveries at-least-once and require receiver idempotency. Store attempts and terminal failures durably; cap attempts and age, then move to a dead-letter/failed state. Manual replay should be permissioned, audited, rate-limited, and subject to the current URL and egress checks."
